title: Follow-ups from the #776 reviews: records and rules that still name the Air or disagree, and iOS CI vs a running dev:api
acceptance: Open records that still give the Air a job are updated: RF-191's title ("Air runs it"), RF-224's next action (the next web deploy "(the Air)"), RF-183's signed-in checks by "the Air conductor" with the QA token (RF-155), including where that token now lives, and RF-179's "next docs PR on the Air".
two-machine-rules.md › 7.4 step 2 no longer cites the night's claim from §2's "Both machines on" bullet, which waits for a second machine; the claim rule sits where a one-machine night reads it.

A daytime rule, or a recorded owner decision not to add one: with web dev and the iOS CI runner on the same Neo, a pnpm dev:api left running from a web branch would serve iOS CI's localhost:8787 auth tests (two-machine-rules.md › 7.6 covers unattended nights only).
two-machine-rules.md's header says the iOS parity check warns ("copy owed from web") when the vendored copy drifts, not that it fails, as iOS AGENTS.md says (owner decision, 2026-11-04).
Web CLAUDE.md's Two conductors bullet says the Neo holds the owner's wrangler login, not its conductor.
AGENTS.md › Never granted, or a recorded owner answer, says whether a Worker rollback counts as a deploy (the owner's yes in the session) or may run without it.

The runbook's "If the Neo can't roll back" fallback ("a machine where the owner is signed in to Cloudflare") agrees with two-machine-rules.md › 1 ("No other machine holds Cloudflare credentials of any kind"); this widens RF-179's rollback item.
nextAction: Backlog until the owner sets it Ready.
